alerts.title: Low phosphate with TDF suggests tubular toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list tubular wasting syndrome as a TDF adverse effect and recommend eGFR monitoring at 3, 6, then 6–12 months. Patient on TDF for 6 years has low serum phosphate (0.78 mmol/L) and trace proteinuria, both consistent with proximal tubular dysfunction. Creatinine is 112 umol/L, which the clinician calls normal, but no eGFR is documented. Evidence for drug attribution: TDF is a known cause of phosphate wasting and proteinuria, and ibuprofen use may potentiate renal injury. Evidence against: hypertension alone can cause trace proteinuria, and occupational factors may contribute. However, hypophosphataemia is not explained by hypertension.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR. If tubular dysfunction confirmed, consider switching TDF to TAF or alternative. Avoid nephrotoxins including regular ibuprofen. Monitor phosphate and proteinuria.

alerts.title: Ibuprofen plus TDF and hypertension increases renal risk
alerts.message: Guidelines note TDF can cause renal failure and tubular wasting, and that intercurrent illness with dehydration may worsen renal function in TDF patients. Patient uses over-the-counter ibuprofen PRN for back pain while on TDF, with hypertension (BP 146/94), trace proteinuria, and low phosphate. NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion and can compound TDF-associated nephrotoxicity. The clinician's plan recommends continuing PRN ibuprofen without flagging this risk. No renal protective alternative for pain is addressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Advise limiting or avoiding ibuprofen. Consider paracetamol-based pain management. Monitor renal function and phosphate closely given concurrent TDF use.

alerts.title: eGFR not documented despite TDF and renal risk factors
alerts.message: Guidelines require eGFR monitoring before TDF initiation, at 3 and 6 months, then 6–12 monthly, and advise avoiding TDF if eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73m². Patient has been on TDF for 6 years with hypertension and trace proteinuria, yet no eGFR is recorded today. Creatinine of 112 umol/L alone is insufficient for safe monitoring. High-risk patients with co-existent hypertension warrant closer renal surveillance.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate and document eGFR at this visit. Given hypertension and proteinuria, schedule renal monitoring at least every 6 months.

alerts.title: Uncontrolled BP with trace proteinuria needs escalation
alerts.message: Guidelines list lower limb oedema as a common amlodipine side effect requiring observation. Patient has BP 146/94 despite amlodipine 5 mg, with admitted non-adherence and trace proteinuria attributed to hypertension. The plan only refills the same dose without escalation or urinalysis follow-up. Persistent hypertension with proteinuria may worsen renal function, compounding TDF nephrotoxicity risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Address adherence barriers. Consider amlodipine dose increase to 10 mg or add a second antihypertensive. Recheck BP and proteinuria sooner than 6 months.
